roll-rudiments.title: Roll Rudiments
roll-rudiments.blurb: Fifteen rudiments built from single strokes, multiple-bounce strokes, and double strokes. The double-stroke family — the “numbered” rolls — is named for the total stroke count, roll plus release.

diddle-rudiments.title: Diddle Rudiments
diddle-rudiments.blurb: The paradiddle family: singles and doubles mixed inside one phrase. The diddle placement flips or holds the lead hand, which is what makes these patterns so useful for moving accents around the kit.

flam-rudiments.title: Flam Rudiments
flam-rudiments.blurb: Eleven rudiments decorated with a single grace note. The grace is played low and soft an instant before the main stroke — one thick sound, never two equal notes.

drag-rudiments.title: Drag Rudiments
drag-rudiments.blurb: Ten rudiments decorated with a two-note grace — the drag (or ruff). The two grace notes are played as a soft diddle by the opposite hand, crushed in just before the main stroke.

1.name: Single Stroke Roll
1.description: Alternating strokes — R L R L — perfectly even in volume and spacing. Every fill and every fast run around the kit traces back to this motion.

card.description: Alternating strokes — R L R L — perfectly even in volume and spacing. Every fill and every fast run around the kit traces back to this motion.

2.name: Single Stroke Four
2.description: Four alternating strokes phrased as a triplet flowing into a downbeat — R L R L. The classic figure for punctuating the end of a fill.

card.description: Four alternating strokes phrased as a triplet flowing into a downbeat — R L R L. The classic figure for punctuating the end of a fill.

3.name: Single Stroke Seven
3.description: Seven alternating strokes — a sextuplet flowing into a downbeat. The single stroke four’s bigger sibling, filling a whole beat before it lands.

card.description: Seven alternating strokes — a sextuplet flowing into a downbeat. The single stroke four’s bigger sibling, filling a whole beat before it lands.

4.name: Multiple Bounce Roll
4.description: The buzz roll: each stroke is pressed into the head so the stick bounces many times, and the alternating buzzes overlap into one continuous sound.

card.description: The buzz roll: each stroke is pressed into the head so the stick bounces many times, and the alternating buzzes overlap into one continuous sound.

5.name: Triple Stroke Roll
5.description: Three strokes per hand in triplet time — R R R L L L. Builds the controlled multi-rebound behind fast open rolls.

card.description: Three strokes per hand in triplet time — R R R L L L. Builds the controlled multi-rebound behind fast open rolls.

6.name: Double Stroke Open Roll
6.description: Two even strokes per hand — R R L L. The parent of every numbered roll below; the second note of each pair must match the first, not collapse.

card.description: Two even strokes per hand — R R L L. The parent of every numbered roll below; the second note of each pair must match the first, not collapse.

7.name: Five Stroke Roll
7.description: Two diddles and an accented release — R R L L R. The shortest numbered roll; the lead alternates so both hands learn to start it.

card.description: Two diddles and an accented release — R R L L R. The shortest numbered roll; the lead alternates so both hands learn to start it.

8.name: Six Stroke Roll
8.description: A diddled middle framed by two accented singles — R L L R R L. A kit favorite because the accents fall naturally on strong beats.

card.description: A diddled middle framed by two accented singles — R L L R R L. A kit favorite because the accents fall naturally on strong beats.

9.name: Seven Stroke Roll
9.description: Three diddles resolving onto an accent — R R L L R R L. Classically starts on an upbeat and lands on the following downbeat.

card.description: Three diddles resolving onto an accent — R R L L R R L. Classically starts on an upbeat and lands on the following downbeat.

10.name: Nine Stroke Roll
10.description: Four diddles capped by an accent — two full beats of roll before the release. The workhorse concert roll.

card.description: Four diddles capped by an accent — two full beats of roll before the release. The workhorse concert roll.

11.name: Ten Stroke Roll
11.description: Four diddles plus two accented singles — R R L L R R L L R L. The double accent at the end gives it its skipping character.

card.description: Four diddles plus two accented singles — R R L L R R L L R L. The double accent at the end gives it its skipping character.

12.name: Eleven Stroke Roll
12.description: Five diddles resolving to an accent — R R L L R R L L R R L. The odd length flips the lead each repeat, keeping both hands honest.

card.description: Five diddles resolving to an accent — R R L L R R L L R R L. The odd length flips the lead each repeat, keeping both hands honest.

13.name: Thirteen Stroke Roll
13.description: Six diddles and the release — three full beats of roll landing accented on beat four.

card.description: Six diddles and the release — three full beats of roll landing accented on beat four.

14.name: Fifteen Stroke Roll
14.description: Seven diddles into the accent — a bar-length roll that releases on the final upbeat.

card.description: Seven diddles into the accent — a bar-length roll that releases on the final upbeat.

15.name: Seventeen Stroke Roll
15.description: Eight diddles — two beats of roll at doubled density — released onto an accented downbeat. The longest of the standard rolls.

card.description: Eight diddles — two beats of roll at doubled density — released onto an accented downbeat. The longest of the standard rolls.

16.name: Single Paradiddle
16.description: The essential single–double hybrid — R L R R, L R L L — accent on the first note. The diddle flips the lead every group, so accents alternate hands automatically.

card.description: The essential single–double hybrid — R L R R, L R L L — accent on the first note. The diddle flips the lead every group, so accents alternate hands automatically.

17.name: Double Paradiddle
17.description: Four singles and a diddle — R L R L R R — six notes that sit perfectly inside triplet meters and 6/8 grooves.

card.description: Four singles and a diddle — R L R L R R — six notes that sit perfectly inside triplet meters and 6/8 grooves.

18.name: Triple Paradiddle
18.description: Six singles and a diddle — an eight-note paradiddle spanning two full beats. A great drill for carrying an accent across a longer phrase.

card.description: Six singles and a diddle — an eight-note paradiddle spanning two full beats. A great drill for carrying an accent across a longer phrase.

19.name: Single Paradiddle-Diddle
19.description: A paradiddle with a second diddle — R L R R L L. Unlike the single paradiddle it does not flip the lead, so practice it starting from both hands.

card.description: A paradiddle with a second diddle — R L R R L L. Unlike the single paradiddle it does not flip the lead, so practice it starting from both hands.

20.name: Flam
20.description: The grace note itself: a soft tap crushed in just before an accented full stroke. Two notes, one fat sound — the basis of the whole family.

card.description: The grace note itself: a soft tap crushed in just before an accented full stroke. Two notes, one fat sound — the basis of the whole family.

21.name: Flam Accent
21.description: A flam launching each triplet, then two singles — flam-R L R, flam-L R L. The lead alternates every beat.

card.description: A flam launching each triplet, then two singles — flam-R L R, flam-L R L. The lead alternates every beat.

22.name: Flam Tap
22.description: A flammed diddle — the flam plus a tap from the same hand: flam-R R, flam-L L.

card.description: A flammed diddle — the flam plus a tap from the same hand: flam-R R, flam-L L.

23.name: Flamacue
23.description: Four sixteenths and a flammed downbeat, with the accent tucked onto the second note — the off-axis accent is the whole point.

card.description: Four sixteenths and a flammed downbeat, with the accent tucked onto the second note — the off-axis accent is the whole point.

24.name: Flam Paradiddle
24.description: A paradiddle with a flam on the accented first note — flam-R L R R, flam-L R L L.

card.description: A paradiddle with a flam on the accented first note — flam-R L R R, flam-L R L L.

25.name: Single Flammed Mill
25.description: An inverted flam paradiddle — the diddle comes first: flam-R R L R. Keeping the flammed double clean is the challenge.

card.description: An inverted flam paradiddle — the diddle comes first: flam-R R L R. Keeping the flammed double clean is the challenge.

26.name: Flam Paradiddle-Diddle
26.description: The paradiddle-diddle with a flammed lead note — flam-R L R R L L — six notes per beat with the flam alternating hands.

card.description: The paradiddle-diddle with a flammed lead note — flam-R L R R L L — six notes per beat with the flam alternating hands.

27.name: Pataflafla
27.description: “Pa-ta-fla-fla”: flams on the first and fourth sixteenths of every group — flam-R L R flam-L — so two flams land back to back across each join.

card.description: “Pa-ta-fla-fla”: flams on the first and fourth sixteenths of every group — flam-R L R flam-L — so two flams land back to back across each join.

28.name: Swiss Army Triplet
28.description: A flammed diddle plus one single in triplet time — flam-R R L. Sounds like the flam accent but stays under one lead hand, which is why it moves faster.

card.description: A flammed diddle plus one single in triplet time — flam-R R L. Sounds like the flam accent but stays under one lead hand, which is why it moves faster.

29.name: Inverted Flam Tap
29.description: A flam tap turned inside out: the tap comes just before the next flam on the same hand — flam-R L, flam-L R — so the diddle straddles the flam instead of following it.

card.description: A flam tap turned inside out: the tap comes just before the next flam on the same hand — flam-R L, flam-L R — so the diddle straddles the flam instead of following it.

30.name: Flam Drag
30.description: A flam accent whose middle note becomes a drag — flam-R, L-L, R inside each triplet. The drag is written out so you can hear it.

card.description: A flam accent whose middle note becomes a drag — flam-R, L-L, R inside each triplet. The drag is written out so you can hear it.

31.name: Drag
31.description: The two-note grace itself: a soft diddle crushed in before an accented stroke — ll-R, rr-L. Also called the ruff.

card.description: The two-note grace itself: a soft diddle crushed in before an accented stroke — ll-R, rr-L. Also called the ruff.

32.name: Single Drag Tap
32.description: A drag answered by an accented tap on the opposite hand — drag-R, accent L.

card.description: A drag answered by an accented tap on the opposite hand — drag-R, accent L.

33.name: Double Drag Tap
33.description: Two drags before the accented tap — drag-R, drag-R, accent L.

card.description: Two drags before the accented tap — drag-R, drag-R, accent L.

34.name: Lesson 25
34.description: Named for a page in the 1870 Strube drum manual: a drag into two singles with the accent on the last — drag-R L, accent R.

card.description: Named for a page in the 1870 Strube drum manual: a drag into two singles with the accent on the last — drag-R L, accent R.

35.name: Single Dragadiddle
35.description: A paradiddle whose first note is doubled into a drag by the same hand — RR L R R. Unlike a true drag, the double is metered, not crushed.

card.description: A paradiddle whose first note is doubled into a drag by the same hand — RR L R R. Unlike a true drag, the double is metered, not crushed.

36.name: Drag Paradiddle #1
36.description: An accented stroke, then a dragged paradiddle — R, drag-R L R R.

card.description: An accented stroke, then a dragged paradiddle — R, drag-R L R R.

37.name: Drag Paradiddle #2
37.description: An accented stroke and two drags feeding the paradiddle — R, drag-R, drag-R L R R.

card.description: An accented stroke and two drags feeding the paradiddle — R, drag-R, drag-R L R R.

38.name: Single Ratamacue
38.description: “Ra-ta-ma-cue”: a dragged triplet resolving onto an accented downbeat — drag-R L R, accent L.

card.description: “Ra-ta-ma-cue”: a dragged triplet resolving onto an accented downbeat — drag-R L R, accent L.

39.name: Double Ratamacue
39.description: A drag stacked in front of the single ratamacue — drag-R, drag-R L R, accent L.

card.description: A drag stacked in front of the single ratamacue — drag-R, drag-R L R, accent L.

40.name: Triple Ratamacue
40.description: Three drags before the release — drag-R, drag-R, drag-R L R, accent L. The longest of the drag rudiments.

card.description: Three drags before the release — drag-R, drag-R, drag-R L R, accent L. The longest of the drag rudiments.
